mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during and after the rate hike, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) above the prior month's level is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: Unemployment claims show no consistent downward trend after the spike, or 20-day returns are positive or mixed with high p-values.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the HOUST index (residential building permits) for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals building activity and economic momentum.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 60-day window following the three-month trend, or the effect is spurious (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 2% is associated with a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return due to weak manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >=2% in a month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are non-negative or the relationship is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 20-day rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as labor market tightness supports equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain flat or negative during the two-month tightness, or the effect is not robust across regimes.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels jointly predict a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return through improved consumer and business demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous month AND RSAFS > previous month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days despite both proxies rising, or interaction p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of over 0.5% followed by a stabilization suggests inflation control, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return in non-recession regimes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops by >0.5% in a month then remains flat for the next month
failure_condition: No positive 60-day return occurs after the CPI pattern, or inflation spikes again within 60 days invalidating the regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in GDPC1 (GDP) is negative for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to persistent economic softness.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 20-day window.
